lenses.name: XF 8-16mm F2.8 R LM WR
lenses.infinity_notes: Focus-by-wire linear motor AF; no documented hard stop.
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Bulbous front complicates dew-heater fit; barrel widens toward the front element.
lenses.coma_notes: Photography Life's review calls it a professional-grade ultra-wide zoom with field-curvature correction; a premium option at the top of the Fujifilm X wide-zoom line.
lenses.popularity_evidence: Fujifilm's flagship fast APS-C ultra-wide zoom; commonly recommended for Milky Way and landscape astro work on X-mount.

lenses.name: XF 8mm F3.5 R WR
lenses.infinity_notes: Focus-by-wire; no documented hard stop.
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Small, evenly cylindrical barrel; dew-heater friendly.
lenses.coma_notes: Slower f/3.5 aperture limits Milky Way suitability compared to faster options; included for completeness as Fujifilm's smallest/lightest rectilinear ultra-wide (12mm-equivalent).
lenses.popularity_evidence: Notable mainly for being the smallest and lightest ultra-wide rectilinear prime in the Fujifilm X lineup; a travel/backup option rather than a primary fast astro lens.

lenses.name: E 11mm F1.8
lenses.infinity_notes: Focus-by-wire dual linear-motor AF; no documented hard stop.
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Very small, uniformly cylindrical barrel; easy dew-heater fit.
lenses.coma_notes: DustinAbbott.net's review calls it a "tiny beast" with strong optical performance for its size; widely used as a compact fast APS-C wide-angle for Milky Way work.
lenses.popularity_evidence: One of Sony's few native fast APS-C wide primes; commonly recommended for a6000/a6700-series Milky Way shooters.

lenses.name: 9mm f/2.8 Zero-D
lenses.infinity_notes: All-manual with a conventional distance scale and hard stop at infinity.
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Small, evenly cylindrical manual-focus barrel; dew-heater friendly.
lenses.coma_notes: Marketed and reviewed as the world's widest rectilinear f/2.8 lens for mirrorless APS-C at launch; Digital Camera World's review notes strong distortion control (Zero-D) though no dedicated coma/astigmatism figure captured in this pass.
lenses.popularity_evidence: Frequently recommended in APS-C ultra-wide astro-landscape guides for its extreme field of view (13mm full-frame equivalent) at a fast, usable aperture.

lenses.name: 7.5mm f/2 Fisheye
lenses.infinity_notes: All-manual with a conventional distance scale and hard stop.
lenses.dew_heater_notes: All-metal cylindrical barrel behind the fisheye front bulge.
lenses.coma_notes: A budget circular-image-style fisheye popular for 180° (150° on MFT) creative Milky Way arcs; no dedicated coma test captured in this pass since fisheye designs are evaluated differently from rectilinear coma testing.
lenses.popularity_evidence: Common budget fisheye pick for APS-C and MFT astro-landscape shooters wanting extreme, distorted wide-field Milky Way compositions.

lenses.name: 6.5mm f/2 Circular Fisheye
lenses.infinity_notes: All-manual budget lens; hard-stop behavior not independently confirmed in sourced pages, left null.
lenses.filters: No filter support (circular fisheye front element).
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Small barrel behind a protruding circular-fisheye front element; dew heating is impractical on this lens shape.
lenses.coma_notes: Produces a full circular (not full-frame) image with a 190° field of view — a specialty creative/scientific format, not a typical rectilinear Milky Way lens; no coma test applicable in the conventional sense.
lenses.popularity_evidence: A very low-cost circular-fisheye novelty lens occasionally used for all-sky/star-trail circular compositions; niche rather than mainstream Milky Way use.

lenses.name: Sniper 16mm F1.2 AF
lenses.infinity_notes: STM AF, focus-by-wire; no documented hard stop.
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Cylindrical barrel; dew-heater friendly.
lenses.coma_notes: Very fast f/1.2 aperture is notable for a budget APS-C prime; no dedicated coma/astigmatism test captured in this pass, so optical night-sky performance is unverified beyond general reviews (CineD, Camera Jabber) covering general image quality, not astro-specific testing.
lenses.popularity_evidence: New entrant (2024) gaining attention for its unusually fast f/1.2 aperture at a budget price point; included as an emerging option rather than an established astro favorite.

lenses.name: 7.5mm f/2 MFT
lenses.infinity_notes: All-manual with a conventional distance scale and hard stop, typical of Laowa's manual-focus line.
lenses.weight_notes: 170 g standard version, 150 g lightweight version.
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Very small, evenly cylindrical barrel; dew-heater friendly.
lenses.coma_notes: Equivalent to 15mm full-frame field of view; long-standing favorite compact fast MFT wide-angle for astro-landscape work, widely covered in MFT gear guides though no dedicated numeric coma test was captured in this pass.
lenses.popularity_evidence: One of the most recommended fast wide-angle primes for Micro Four Thirds astro-landscape shooters due to its light weight and 15mm-equivalent field of view.

lenses.name: M.Zuiko Digital ED 8mm F1.8 Fisheye PRO
lenses.infinity_notes: AF with manual focus clutch/ring; hard-stop behavior not independently confirmed in sourced pages, left null.
lenses.filters: No front filter thread (fisheye front element); rear filter capability not confirmed in this pass.
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Weather-sealed PRO-series barrel; fisheye front bulge complicates dew-heater fit.
lenses.coma_notes: Fast f/1.8 aperture on a 16mm-equivalent circular/diagonal fisheye design is popular for MFT astro-landscape shooters wanting an ultra-wide fast option; no dedicated coma test captured in this pass (fisheye designs are evaluated differently from rectilinear coma testing).
lenses.popularity_evidence: The reference fast fisheye for Micro Four Thirds astro-landscape work, frequently recommended in MFT-specific astro gear guides for its unique combination of speed and field of view.

lenses.name: Leica DG Vario-Summilux 10-25mm F1.7 ASPH
lenses.infinity_notes: Focus-by-wire; no documented hard stop.
lenses.filters: Front filter thread present per manufacturer (size not independently confirmed in this pass).
lenses.dew_heater_notes: Weather-sealed cylindrical barrel; among the largest/heaviest lenses in this MFT list, still dew-heater friendly.
lenses.coma_notes: A constant-f/1.7 standard zoom (20–50mm equivalent) rather than an ultra-wide astro prime; included for completeness as a popular fast MFT zoom sometimes used for wider Milky Way framing at its 10mm end. No dedicated coma test captured in this pass.
lenses.popularity_evidence: One of the fastest constant-aperture zooms in any current mirrorless system; popular among MFT shooters wanting one do-everything fast lens, including night work at its wide end.
